name: Erdafitinib (FGFR2/3-altered)

biomarkers.FGFR: susceptible FGFR2 or FGFR3 genetic/genomic alteration (REQUIRED)
biomarkers.note: BIOMARKER-GATED: erdafitinib is an oral pan-FGFR (FGFR1-4) tyrosine kinase inhibitor indicated ONLY for urothelial carcinoma harboring a susceptible FGFR3 (and per label FGFR2/3) genomic alteration. FGFR testing is mandatory before use. Applies to bladder (#57) and upper-tract (#58) urothelial carcinoma. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G 5 of 8, biomarker-directed therapy, category 1 after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor); DeVita 12th ed. line 23438 (erdafitinib for FGFR2/3-altered bladder cancer).

lineOfTherapy: subsequent-line for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with a susceptible FGFR2/3 alteration, after prior platinum-based chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: susceptible FGFR2 or FGFR3 genomic alteration confirmed by a validated assay (REQUIRED)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v3.2026, BL-G 5 of 8 (Erdafitinib for susceptible FGFR3 genetic/genomic alterations; category 1 after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor); DeVita 12th ed. line 23438 (FGFR2/3-altered bladder cancer)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: prior platinum-based chemotherapy and a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor (for the category 1 recommendation)

drugs.name: Erdafitinib

provenance.locator: VERIFY - the erdafitinib dose (intended 8 mg PO once daily, with up-titration to 9 mg based on day 14-21 serum phosphate per BLC2001/THOR) is NOT printed in the provided licensed sources. DeVita 12th ed. line 23438 and Harrison identify erdafitinib for FGFR2/3-altered bladder cancer but do not print the mg dose. Do not infer.

drugs.notes: VERIFY: erdafitinib is given orally once daily continuously (intended 8 mg PO daily, with pharmacodynamic up-titration to 9 mg based on serum phosphate at day 14-21 per BLC2001/THOR). The mg dose and phosphate-driven up-titration are NOT dose-grounded in the provided sources, so dosePerUnit is set to VERIFY (never invented) and must be resolved against a cited source before use.

supportiveCare: HYPERPHOSPHATEMIA: serum phosphate is an on-target pharmacodynamic effect and drives dose up-titration; monitor phosphate, restrict dietary phosphate and use phosphate binders as needed.
OCULAR: central serous retinopathy / retinal pigment epithelial detachment can occur; baseline and periodic ophthalmologic exams (including OCT); counsel on visual symptoms.
Monitor for nail toxicity, stomatitis, dry mouth/skin, and hand-foot syndrome.
FGFR testing must be confirmed before initiation.

monitoring: ophthalmologic exam / OCT (central serous retinopathy) at baseline and periodically
nail and mucocutaneous toxicity (stomatitis, nail changes, hand-foot syndrome)

doseModificationRules.text: Manage hyperphosphatemia with dietary phosphate restriction and phosphate binders; hold and reduce erdafitinib per labeling if phosphate remains elevated. Up-titration and reduction thresholds cannot be finalized until the starting dose (VERIFY) is resolved.
Hold erdafitinib and obtain urgent ophthalmologic evaluation for new visual symptoms or central serous retinopathy; resume or discontinue per severity.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: line 23438 (erdafitinib, a pan-FGFR inhibitor for FGFR2/3-altered bladder cancer); lines 22149-22158 (erdafitinib) - dose not printed

guideline.locator: Principles of Systemic Therapy, biomarker-directed therapy (BL-G 5 of 8, line 309): Erdafitinib for susceptible FGFR3 genetic/genomic alterations, category 1 for patients who have already received platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor. Dosing not printed in the guideline.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for erdafitinib in FGFR2/3-altered locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (bladder #57, upper-tract #58). This is a BIOMARKER-GATED regimen: a susceptible FGFR2/3 genomic alteration is REQUIRED and recorded in both biomarkers and eligibilityCriteria, grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Bladder Cancer v3.2026 (BL-G 5 of 8, category 1 after platinum and a checkpoint inhibitor) and DeVita 12th ed. line 23438. The dose (intended 8 mg PO daily with up-titration to 9 mg by serum phosphate per BLC2001/THOR) is NOT printed in the provided licensed sources, so dosePerUnit is set to VERIFY and never inferred (verifyFields records the paths). Erdafitinib-specific safety (on-target hyperphosphatemia driving up-titration, central serous retinopathy, nail/mucocutaneous toxicity) is captured. This regimen is NOT dose-groundable from the current sources and must not be used until the dose is resolved. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
